definitions.meaning: read as '...', the gunslinger who is quickest on the draw
... describes the very highest social class

explanation.surface: Who is the quickest gun among the smart set?
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into TOP DRAWER, one who draws a gun best; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for upper-class, of the finest social standing, and the split phrase pictures a champion gunslinger.

parts.note: taken as written
to gain something is to win it
G is the physics symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: Something hauling a load in order to acquire weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Towing a vehicle means hauling it behind you, a synonym of pulling.

clue.text: Nothing more than a discreet Tory perhaps

indicators.note: more than signals that the nothing letter is added on after the word for discreet

parts.note: politic means prudent or discreet
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A quiet Conservative is nothing more than tactful.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of a political party, an example of a career politician.

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
Ted, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy from Rio went on the rampage.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot is to run wild in a violent disturbance, much as a rampaging mob does.

clue.text: Decant wine with hesitation before the German veal cutlet

indicators.note: decanting pours the wine out, so its letters are poured into a new order

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pours the wine haltingly before serving a schnitzel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decant' pours the wine letters into a new order; 'before the' is a link. The word is short for Wiener schnitzel, a Viennese dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiener schnitzel is a breaded slice of veal, a dish associated with German-speaking cooking.

definitions.meaning: a nick is a small cut, such as one made shaving
a haircut thinned and shaped with a blade

explanation.surface: Nick has a short tapered haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name owning a haircut; it is a small cut, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick while shaving is a blade wound, and the same phrase names a hairstyle shaped with a blade instead of scissors.

clue.text: Is returning with previously unknown strength

indicators.note: returning means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: something new was not known before

explanation.surface: Strength that comes back is something fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and figuratively muscular power or vigour.

indicators.note: distributing scatters things, so the letters of seed-corn are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer backing the sowing of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder backs a motion at a meeting, endorsing the proposer.

clue.text: Off about one? That's the idea

indicators.note: about says the words for off go round the one

parts.note: an event that is off is not on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is off about one thing, and that's the thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, a synonym of idea.

parts.note: a worm such as a tapeworm lives as a parasite
to cast up figures is an old way of saying add them

explanation.surface: A parasite adds to the heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link; cast meaning add, as in casting accounts, is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A wormcast is the little coil of earth an earthworm leaves on the surface, a tiny heap.

definitions.meaning: a salutation offered to an arrival
describing a guest or news that is gladly accepted

explanation.definitionFit: Welcome is both the friendly reception given on arrival and an adjective for something gladly accepted.

parts.note: suggests freshly minted money, but means a newly invented word

explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly made-up word, and coining is the usual verb for inventing words.

clue.text: Smile in front of the German student who is hard-working

indicators.note: in front of places the smile word before the German article

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A grinning German lad who studies hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinder is slang for a plodding swot who works relentlessly at books.

clue.text: Dance round taking one unknown into virtuoso passage

indicators.note: into places the unknown inside the rearranged letters
round suggests turning about, so dance with an extra letter is rearranged

parts.note: A as the indefinite article means one
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A dance goes round, drawing a mystery figure into a showy musical display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns DANCE plus A into CADENA, and 'into' puts Z inside it; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a showy solo section in a concerto, letting the soloist display brilliance.

parts.note: describes the direction an English reader's eye travels along a line

explanation.definitionFit: English text runs from the left margin to the right, the direction of reading.

parts.note: sounds like something that kills a swimmer, but means the rear end of an aquatic creature

explanation.definitionFit: The rear fin of an aquatic animal is literally the end of its body.

clue.text: Body of delegates transferred to Ealing

indicators.note: transferred suggests moving, so the letters of to Ealing are moved around

explanation.surface: A diplomatic body was relocated to Ealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A legation is a diplomatic mission headed by a minister, a group of envoys.

clue.text: Sets of chemical symbols, make universal list as explained initially

parts.note: to form something is to make it
U is the abbreviation for universal, the British film rating

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: Chemistry notation instructions: build a general list as first explained.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical formulas such as H2O show compounds in symbols; the plural is often written with the Latin ending.

definitions.meaning: comprehending, as in getting the idea

explanation.definitionFit: Grasping means avaricious, and as a participle it means comprehending, as when one grasps a point.

definitions.meaning: to lurch from side to side

explanation.surface: A music genre's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the music genre, but each word separately means to totter; 'n' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to walk unsteadily, swaying and lurching like a ship in heavy seas.

clue.text: Keen discernment of bill with revised menu

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: revised means the letters of menu are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner shrewdly checks the bill against an amended menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharpness of judgment, especially in business, a close synonym of insight.

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of Hardy are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
NT, the New Testament, is a book of scripture

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's latest novel needs a publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link. Thomas Hardy was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire hydrant is a street pipe with a nozzle from which water can be drawn, an outlet for the mains.

clue.text: Go into this for a secret conference

definitions.text: Go into this for a secret conference

parts.words: Go into this for a secret conference
parts.note: players or plotters gather close together to talk privately

explanation.definitionFit: Players in American football gather in a tight circle to agree plays out of earshot, a private conflab.

parts.note: sounds like a company directors' session, but means the chief meal at the table, board being an old word for table

explanation.definitionFit: The principal meal of the day is eaten together at the table, once called the board.

clue.text: Just the thing for a collector

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'that's just the ...' means exactly what is wanted
what an inspector on a train or at a turnstile takes from passengers

explanation.definitionFit: A travel pass is what a conductor collects, and the idiom 'just the ...' means exactly right.

clue.text: Kitty to rely first on money held in managed estate

indicators.note: first on places the word for rely ahead of the word for kitty

parts.note: to trust is to rely on
a kitty is a pooled fund of money

explanation.surface: A family pot left to someone to rely on, held in a run estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets held by trustees on behalf of a beneficiary are money in a managed estate.

clue.text: Dull brown Scottish church in France

definitions.note: the definition names a place located in France

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
kirk is the Scots word for a church

explanation.surface: A drab brown Scottish chapel stands on French soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in France' stands for a town there, the Channel port famous for the 1940 evacuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern French port, site of the Allied evacuation in 1940.

clue.text: Name attached to string on laundry items

indicators.note: attached to places the name letter after the string word

parts.note: a line is a length of string or cord

explanation.surface: Name tags sewn onto a string of washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen covers sheets, tablecloths and towels, the household textiles that go to the wash.

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: the pronoun spoken sounds like the organ of sight
bright means cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone claims to own a cheerful plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright, Euphrasia, is a small wild flower once used to treat eye complaints.
